behaviours.excerpt: Halcyon’s relevant figures are: 8.1 company-wide thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year, including 4 incidents not reported to a regulator; our flagship’s 55 °C test failure rate is 3.9%, and its incident rate is 9.9 per 100,000.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every confirmed thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account of known risks and response steps. Within 72 hours of learning of an incident, manufacturers must notify the affected unit’s customer of known immediate safety steps and how to obtain updates.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Exceeding 5% triggers regulatory review but does not by itself require an automatic ban; the regulator may require additional safeguards, restrict sales, or take other proportionate action based on the results and evidence of risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For units already installed when this standard is adopted, manufacturers must enable remote shut-off where technically supported within six years; where it is not supported, they must notify customers and provide an equivalent safe shut-off procedure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems manufactured 36 months or more after adoption of this standard must include built-in fire suppression appropriate to the system’s chemistry and installation, validated under a regulator-approved test protocol. Regulators may approve an equivalent protective design where it provides comparable mitigation of fire spread and risk to occupants and neighbours.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period; the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop new sales pending regulator review, and implement the regulator-approved recall or corrective action.

document.section_notes: The final text keeps the 5% per-model test limit but removes any sales stop for exceeding it, relying on regulatory review, which largely protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). The remote shut-off retrofit runs six years, matching Northwind's 38% installed shut-off capability, while S4 suppression starts at 36 months, which benefits Halcyon's cost position. S5 sets a mandatory 8-per-100k recall trigger with no transition, but its open-ended corrective-action alternative gives a route around recall for Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9.
